options.name: Departure briefing and welcome reception
options.difficulty_note: Seated and standing at a reception. No walking.
options.description: Tonight the expedition begins. Over a drink, you meet the people who will share the next 25 days, hear how the journey unfolds, and look at the map that is about to turn into memories. Ask everything you want. By the end of the evening, the round-the-world flight will feel real.
options.bring: Smart casual.
options.accessibility: On one level, seated or standing, with a lift from the lobby to the ballroom floor. Step-free.

options.name: Altitude orientation walk
options.difficulty_note: A slow 1 km stroll on flat ground at 3,400 m above sea level. The air is thin: go slowly and drink water.
options.description: Today we take our first slow steps at 3,400 metres. We wander the old streets of Cusco at the pace of the thin air, stop in a sunlit courtyard for a cup of coca tea, and let our bodies learn the Andes. It is the gentlest way to start one of the great adventures of the trip.
options.bring: High altitude: go slowly and rest when you need to. The sun is strong and the weather changes quickly: layers and a rain jacket.
options.accessibility: Flat ground on cobbled streets, no steps, at 3,400 m. Wheelchairs can follow the route but cobbles are uneven and the air is thin.

options.name: Sacred Valley: Chinchero
options.difficulty_note: About 3 km of walking on uneven ground and Inca stone steps, at around 3,800 m. Some short climbs. The weaving demonstration is seated.
options.description: Today we climb into the Andean sky to Chinchero, a weaver's village older than the Inca. Women in bright shawls show us how wool is dyed with plants, crushed insects and flowers, then spun and woven by hand. We walk the terraces the Inca built, step into a church painted by candlelight, and leave with the feeling of having been welcomed into a living tradition.
options.bring: High altitude: go slowly and rest when you need to. The sun is strong and the weather changes quickly: layers and a rain jacket.
options.accessibility: Some steps or uneven ground. Guests with limited mobility should speak to their guide before choosing this tour.

options.name: Maras and Moray
options.difficulty_note: About 2 km of walking in total, with steps down into the Moray terraces (optional) and uneven paths at the salt pans, at around 3,500 m.
options.description: Today we visit two places that look like they came from another world. At Moray, circular terraces sink into the earth like a giant amphitheatre, perhaps the Inca's open-air laboratory. At Maras, thousands of shimmering salt pools still glitter on the mountainside, worked by families for centuries. Bring your camera; the light here is extraordinary.
options.bring: High altitude: go slowly and rest when you need to. The sun is strong and the weather changes quickly: layers and a rain jacket.
options.accessibility: Some steps or uneven ground. Guests with limited mobility should speak to their guide before choosing this tour.

options.name: Cusco City Tour
options.difficulty_note: Short walks on cobbled streets with a few steps, at 3,400 m. Frequent stops. Coach between sites.
options.description: Today we walk through the heart of the Inca empire. On the Plaza de Armas we learn how a capital shaped like a puma became a Spanish city, and at the Coricancha, once plated in gold, we see Inca stonework so precise that no blade fits between the blocks. The story of two worlds colliding is written in these walls.
options.bring: High altitude: go slowly and rest when you need to. The sun is strong and the weather changes quickly: layers and a rain jacket.
options.accessibility: The cathedral and the Coricancha are step-free at the entrances, with a few steps inside. The Plaza de Armas is flat but cobbled. Several uneven stone floors.

options.name: Sacsayhuaman
options.difficulty_note: About 2 km on grass and uneven stone at 3,700 m, with a climb of about 100 m. Slow pace.
options.description: Today we stand beneath the walls of Sacsayhuaman, a fortress built with stones that weigh as much as a lorry, fitted together without mortar. Our guide tells how it was built, how it fell, and why Cusco still looks up to it. From the top, the whole red-roofed city lies at our feet.
options.bring: High altitude: go slowly and rest when you need to. The sun is strong and the weather changes quickly: layers and a rain jacket.
options.accessibility: The site is on a slope, with grass and stone steps up to the platform and no lift. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Machu Picchu by train
options.difficulty_note: A train ride, a bus up the mountain, then about 3 km of walking with many stone steps on the citadel, at 2,400 m. Long day. A guide can set a slower pace.
options.description: Today we board the scenic train that follows the roaring Urubamba river into the cloud forest, and then, at last, we climb to the lost city of the Incas. Machu Picchu appears out of the mist, terraces draped over the mountain, and our guide leads us through temples and royal rooms. It is the day many of us have dreamed about for years.
options.bring: High altitude: go slowly and rest when you need to. The sun is strong and the weather changes quickly: layers and a rain jacket.
options.accessibility: The train has level boarding with a step; luggage racks are narrow. Inside the site there are about 250 stone steps up to the main viewpoints and no handrails in places. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Ahu Tahai at sunset
options.difficulty_note: Flat, short walk on grass. Windy.
options.description: Today we meet the moai at the best hour of the day. As the sun sinks into the Pacific, the restored statues of Ahu Tahai glow gold, and a local Rapa Nui guide tells the story of the people who carved them and carried them across the island. There is nothing between you and the horizon. Stay for the last light.
options.bring: Very windy and exposed: a windproof jacket. Do not climb on or touch the statues or the platforms.
options.accessibility: Mostly level and gentle: suitable for most guests, including those who walk slowly. Tell your guide if you use a wheelchair or a walker and we will check access for you.

options.name: Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki
options.difficulty_note: About 3 km on grass and uneven volcanic ground, with a climb of about 60 m at the quarry. Little shade, strong sun and wind.
options.description: Today we walk into the quarry where the moai were born. Nearly 400 statues, some finished, some half-carved, stare out from the slopes of Rano Raraku as if the sculptors had just put down their tools. Then, at Ahu Tongariki, fifteen giants stand in a row facing the sea. It is one of the most powerful sights on Earth.
options.bring: Very windy and exposed: a windproof jacket. Do not climb on or touch the statues or the platforms.
options.accessibility: Some steps or uneven ground. Guests with limited mobility should speak to their guide before choosing this tour.

options.name: Anakena beach and Ahu Nau Nau
options.difficulty_note: Flat, soft sand. Swimming is optional.
options.description: Today we visit the one white-sand beach on Easter Island, the place where, legend says, the first king landed. Palm trees sway behind the moai of Ahu Nau Nau, the best-preserved on the island, some still wearing their red topknots. Swim, walk, and imagine the canoes arriving a thousand years ago.
options.bring: The sun is strong: hat and sun cream. Swimwear and a towel if you want to swim.
options.accessibility: Mostly level and gentle: suitable for most guests, including those who walk slowly. Tell your guide if you use a wheelchair or a walker and we will check access for you.

options.name: Orongo ceremonial village
options.difficulty_note: A drive to the crater rim, then about 1 km on a flat path. Strong wind; keep to the path near the edge.
options.description: Today we stand on the rim of a crater, 300 metres above the sea, where young men once raced to bring back the first egg of the sooty tern. Among the stone houses of Orongo, petroglyphs of the birdman look out over the islets, and the wind tells the story. The view alone is worth the journey.
options.bring: Very windy and exposed: a windproof jacket. Do not climb on or touch the statues or the platforms.
options.accessibility: Mostly level and gentle: suitable for most guests, including those who walk slowly. Tell your guide if you use a wheelchair or a walker and we will check access for you.

options.name: Welcome kava ceremony
options.difficulty_note: Seated, on mats on the floor (a chair is available).
options.description: Today a Samoan chief welcomes us the way travellers have been welcomed here for centuries. We sit in a circle, the kava is prepared and passed in a coconut cup, songs rise in the air, and we learn what fa'a Samoa, the Samoan way, truly means. This is not a show. It is an invitation.
options.bring: Smart casual.
options.accessibility: We sit on mats on the floor in a traditional open house. A chair can be provided. One step at the entrance.

options.name: Vailima
options.difficulty_note: A gentle climb of about 40 steps to the house and a flat garden. Hot and humid.
options.description: Today we walk in the footsteps of Robert Louis Stevenson. The author of Treasure Island left Scotland, searching for a place to breathe, and found it on this green hillside above Apia, where the Samoans called him Tusitala, the teller of tales. We tour his house, stroll through the garden he loved, and, if we wish, climb to the hilltop where he chose to be buried, looking out over the Pacific.
options.bring: Hot, humid, and it may rain: a light rain jacket and insect repellent. Stay on the paths.
options.accessibility: The museum is a two-floor house with no lift: the first floor is reached by a flight of about 40 steps with a handrail. The garden is level. The walk to the tomb is optional and takes about 45 minutes uphill on a steep path.

options.name: Women's Committee
options.difficulty_note: Seated on mats for part of the visit (chairs available). Flat ground. Hot and humid.
options.description: Today we are invited into the heart of a Samoan village. The women's committee, which runs the health and daily life of the community, shows us how bark cloth is pounded and painted, how pandanus leaves become fine mats, and how a village takes care of its own. Sit, listen, and perhaps try your hand at weaving.
options.bring: Closed shoes in the kitchen. Tell your guide about any allergy.
options.accessibility: Seating is on mats on the floor; chairs are available on request. The meeting house is one level with a single step at the entrance.

options.name: Lalomanu beach
options.difficulty_note: Flat sand. Swimming is optional. A shaded beach fale is booked for the group.
options.description: Today is for the postcard. A long ribbon of white sand, water in four shades of blue, and fale huts under the palms. Swim, snorkel straight from the shore, and then share a barbecue under the trees with the whole group. Nothing to see. Just everything to feel.
options.bring: The sun is strong: hat and sun cream. Swimwear and a towel if you want to swim.
options.accessibility: Soft sand and a few steps down to the beach. Tables under the trees are on sand. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Great Barrier Reef
options.difficulty_note: About 1.5 hours each way by catamaran, which can be rough. About 2 hours in the water, snorkelling in a life vest or with a noodle. You must be comfortable in open water.
options.description: Today we sail out to the largest living structure on the planet. By catamaran we reach the outer reef, and a marine biologist introduces us to the coral gardens we are about to drift over. Turtles glide past, fish flash in every colour, and lunch is served on deck. You will remember this water for the rest of your life.
options.bring: Swimsuit and a towel. Reef-safe sun cream only. Touching the coral is not allowed.
options.accessibility: You step on and off the catamaran from a pontoon, with crew help, and a ladder or platform to enter the water. Floating aids are provided. Lifts: none. Please tell your leader about any health condition before choosing.

options.name: Daintree Rainforest
options.difficulty_note: About 2 km on boardwalks and gravel paths, hot and humid. A river cruise is seated.
options.description: Today we step into the oldest rainforest on Earth, 180 million years old, older than the Amazon. We glide down a river with our eyes on the banks for crocodiles, then walk a boardwalk through ferns the size of trees, listening for cassowaries. Every sound here is ancient.
options.bring: Hot, humid, and it may rain: a light rain jacket and insect repellent. Stay on the paths.
options.accessibility: The river boat has two steps to board and fixed seats. The boardwalk is flat and wide, about 800 m, with a few ramps and no steps. A wheelchair can use the boardwalk.

options.name: Old Market and Apsara dance
options.difficulty_note: A short, flat walk in a busy market. Hot.
options.description: Today Siem Reap shows us its senses. We wander the Old Market with a local guide, tasting, smelling and bargaining, and in the evening we sit in a candlelit courtyard to watch Apsara dancers, whose gestures have been passed down from the walls of Angkor itself. It is a feast for the eyes.
options.bring: Crowded and busy: keep valuables close. Covered shoulders and knees are appreciated. Ask before photographing people.
options.accessibility: Mostly level and gentle: suitable for most guests, including those who walk slowly. Tell your guide if you use a wheelchair or a walker and we will check access for you.

options.name: Angkor Wat, Ta Prohm, and Angkor Thom
options.difficulty_note: About 4 km of walking on stone, with steep, narrow steps at Angkor Wat (a lower route is available). Very hot from mid-morning. Start is early on purpose.
options.description: Today we explore three wonders of the world in a single day. Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument on Earth, rises from its moat; at Angkor Thom the stone faces of the Bayon smile at us from every tower; and at Ta Prohm, giant tree roots swallow the temple whole. Arrive early. The morning light is magic.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees: these are religious sites. Early start; the sun is strong from mid-morning.
options.accessibility: Angkor Wat has steep stone steps to the upper level (optional, about 70 steps with handrails). Ta Prohm has uneven ground and wooden walkways. Angkor Thom is mostly flat. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Beng Mealea
options.difficulty_note: About 2 km clambering over fallen stones on wooden walkways and uneven ground. A 1 hour 15 minute drive each way. Hot.
options.description: Today we play explorers. Beng Mealea is a vast temple that the jungle has been reclaiming for centuries, and we climb over fallen towers, duck through half-collapsed galleries and follow moss-covered corridors where almost no one else goes. It feels like discovering the temple for the first time.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees: these are religious sites. Early start; the sun is strong from mid-morning.
options.accessibility: Rubble, fallen stones and slippery moss: walking is uneven throughout and climbing is part of the visit. Not suitable for wheelchairs or walking aids.

options.name: Roluos Temple Complex
options.difficulty_note: Short, flat walks between three sites, with a few steps at each. Hot.
options.description: Today we travel back to where Angkor began. The temples of Roluos, Preah Ko, Bakong and Lolei, were built more than a thousand years ago, long before Angkor Wat, and their brick towers and delicate carvings tell the story of the first Khmer capital. Quiet, beautiful, and almost ours alone.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees: these are religious sites. Early start; the sun is strong from mid-morning.
options.accessibility: Short walks on grass and gravel, with a few steep stone steps at each temple (optional). Partly accessible.

options.name: Private Cooking Lesson
options.difficulty_note: Standing at a cooking table, indoors. Flat. Light physical effort.
options.description: Today we cook like a Cambodian family. We pick herbs in a garden, learn the secrets of fresh amok and sour soups from a local chef, and then sit down to eat what we have made. You will leave with a recipe, a full stomach, and a story to retell at home.
options.bring: Closed shoes in the kitchen. Tell your guide about any allergy.
options.accessibility: A covered, open-sided kitchen on level ground. Cooking is done standing or seated on a stool. Suitable for most guests.

options.name: APOPO HeroRATs Visitor Center
options.difficulty_note: Indoors and short flat walks. Light.
options.description: Today we meet the smallest heroes of Cambodia: giant pouched rats trained to sniff out landmines that still lie beneath the soil. We see how they work, meet the people who train them, and learn how every cleared field becomes a school, a farm or a home. It is a story that will stay with you.
options.bring: Comfortable closed shoes. A sun hat in summer.
options.accessibility: One level, ramps at the entrance, and a flat path to the demonstration area. Step-free and suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Angkor Wat, Ta Prohm, and Angkor Thom
options.difficulty_note: About 4 km of walking on stone, with steep, narrow steps at Angkor Wat (a lower route is available). Very hot from mid-morning. Start is early on purpose.

options.accessibility: One level, ramps at the entrance, and a flat path to the demonstration area. Step-free and suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Durbar Square walk
options.difficulty_note: About 2 km on uneven brick paving with a few steps, among crowds and traffic.
options.description: Today we walk through the beating heart of old Kathmandu. Around the royal square, carved wooden temples crowd together, pigeons rise in clouds, and in a small window the Kumari, the living goddess, may appear. Our guide helps us read a city where gods and everyday life share the same streets.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees, and walk clockwise around the stupa. Photography is not allowed in some places: your guide will say where.
options.accessibility: Flat paving in the square, but the temples stand on tall stepped plinths (up to 8 steps) and none have lifts. Narrow lanes and cycle rickshaws. Partly accessible.

options.name: Boudhanath and Pashupatinath
options.difficulty_note: About 3 km on foot over uneven ground and many steps at Pashupatinath. Crowded. The cremation ghats at Pashupatinath may be upsetting for some people; photography is limited.
options.description: Today we meet two sacred places that no one forgets. At Boudhanath, we walk clockwise around one of the biggest stupas in the world, among pilgrims, butter lamps and fluttering prayer flags. At Pashupatinath, on the banks of the Bagmati river, we watch a Hindu temple complex alive with devotion. Open hearts, quiet voices.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees, and walk clockwise around the stupa. Photography is not allowed in some places: your guide will say where.
options.accessibility: The Boudhanath circuit is flat but crowded and paved with worn stones. Pashupatinath has long stairways with no handrails. Partly accessible.

options.name: Thimphu
options.difficulty_note: About 1 hour 30 minutes by coach each way on a winding road. Short, flat walks in the capital. Some people feel carsick on the bends.
options.description: Today we visit the only capital in the world without a single traffic light. In Thimphu, a giant golden Buddha looks out over the valley, a folk heritage museum shows how Bhutanese farm families lived, and the paper-making workshop turns bark into art. A small kingdom with a very big soul.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees. No photographs inside the monastery, and bags are left at the entrance. A warm layer: it is cold at height.
options.accessibility: The Buddha viewing platform is reached by about 20 steps, with a ramp on one side. The heritage museum is a three-floor traditional house with steep wooden stairs and no lift.

options.name: Tiger's Nest Hike
options.difficulty_note: About 10 km round trip with a climb of roughly 900 m, starting at 2,600 m above sea level, so the air is thin. Around 700 uneven steps near the top. Allow 4 hours up and 2 hours down. Not recommended with heart or knee problems or a fear of heights: some stretches are narrow with a drop beside the path. Horses can carry you part of the way up.
options.description: Today we climb to one of the most breathtaking temples ever built. Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest, clings to a cliff 900 metres above the Paro valley, and we reach it on foot through pine forests, prayer flags and a stairway cut into the rock. Hard work. Unforgettable reward. A teahouse waits halfway.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees. No photographs inside the monastery, and bags are left at the entrance. A warm layer: it is cold at height.
options.accessibility: A climb of about 800 m of height over roughly 3 to 4 hours, with some 700 steps near the top and no handrails in places. A pony can help for the first part (extra cost). Not suitable for wheelchairs or for guests with heart or knee problems.

options.name: Agra Fort and Mehtab Bagh sunset
options.difficulty_note: About 1.5 km on flat and slightly sloping stone at the fort. Hot and dusty.
options.description: Today we follow the Mughal emperors. In the red sandstone fort of Agra, we walk the rooms where Shah Jahan, who built the Taj Mahal, was held prisoner, looking out at the monument he loved. Then, in a quiet garden across the river, we wait as the Taj turns from white to gold to pink. It is pure magic.
options.bring: Shoes are removed or covered on the marble. Large bags and tripods are not allowed. Cover shoulders and knees.
options.accessibility: The fort has ramps that are steep and paved with old stone, and some stairs without handrails. The garden is flat and grassy. Partly accessible.

options.name: Taj Mahal at sunrise
options.difficulty_note: About 1.5 km on flat marble and paths. Early start. Shoe covers or bare feet on the marble.
options.description: Today we rise before dawn to meet the world's greatest love story. As the first light touches the marble, the Taj Mahal changes from grey to pearl to rose, and our guide tells of the emperor who built it for his wife. The crowds are small. The silence is huge. This is the moment of the whole trip.
options.bring: Shoes are removed or covered on the marble. Large bags and tripods are not allowed. Cover shoulders and knees.
options.accessibility: The approach is flat, about 600 m from the gate, with 8 steps to the marble platform and a ramp on one side. Shoe covers are provided. Wheelchairs can be used with help.

options.name: Marble inlay workshop
options.difficulty_note: Seated indoors. No walking.
options.description: Today we step into a family workshop where the same craft that decorated the Taj Mahal is still practised. Craftsmen cut tiny pieces of semi-precious stones, shape them by hand and set them into marble with patience that seems to stop time. Watch, ask, and take home a piece of the story.
options.bring: Ask before touching the work. Photography may not be allowed in some workshops.
options.accessibility: A ground-floor workshop with one step at the door. The showroom upstairs is optional and has no lift.

options.name: First game drive
options.difficulty_note: Seated in an open safari vehicle on rough tracks: bumpy, with dust. Getting in and out needs a step.
options.description: Today the Serengeti opens. With a ranger who reads the plains like a book, we drive out into the golden grass, searching for lions in the shade, elephants at the waterhole and giraffes against the sky. Everything is wild, and everything is close. Keep your eyes open and your camera ready.
options.bring: Open vehicle: dust, sun, and cold at dawn. Layers, a hat, neutral colours. Stay seated and quiet near the animals.
options.accessibility: The vehicle has a high step (a stool is provided) and a roof that opens. Seats are fixed and the ride is bumpy. Tell your leader if you use a wheelchair: not every vehicle can carry one.

options.name: Serengeti game drive
options.difficulty_note: Seated in an open vehicle on rough tracks for most of the day. Bumpy, hot and dusty. Picnic lunch in the bush.
options.description: Today we give ourselves a whole day on the plains. We track the great herds with a picnic lunch under an acacia, stop at a hippo pool to watch the grunting giants, and climb a rocky outcrop for a view that goes on forever. This is the Africa you saw in documentaries, and now you are in it.
options.bring: Open vehicle: dust, sun, and cold at dawn. Layers, a hat, neutral colours. Stay seated and quiet near the animals.
options.accessibility: The vehicle has a high step (a stool is provided) and the ride is bumpy over a full day. Toilets are basic bush stops. Tell your leader if you use a wheelchair.

options.name: Ngorongoro Crater Safari
options.difficulty_note: A long drive each way on rough tracks, including a steep descent of about 600 m into the crater by 4x4. Cold at dawn, hot at midday.
options.description: Today we descend into a lost world. The Ngorongoro Crater, the largest intact volcanic caldera on Earth, holds lions, rhinos, hippos, flamingos and thousands of grazers in a single green bowl. We drive down at first light, and by lunchtime we have seen more wildlife than many people see in a lifetime.
options.bring: Very windy and exposed: a windproof jacket. Do not climb on or touch the statues or the platforms.
options.accessibility: The road down the crater wall is steep and winding, and the vehicle step is high (a stool is provided). The drive is long and bumpy. Tell your leader about back problems.

options.name: Olduvai Gorge
options.difficulty_note: A long drive on rough roads and a short walk at the gorge. Seated for the talk in the museum.
options.description: Today we stand in the cradle of humankind. In this dry gorge, scientists found some of the oldest remains of our ancestors, and our guide tells how bones, tools and footprints rewrote the story of who we are. A small museum, a vast idea. You will look at your own hands differently afterwards.
options.bring: Open vehicle: dust, sun, and cold at dawn. Layers, a hat, neutral colours. Stay seated and quiet near the animals.
options.accessibility: The small museum is on one level with a ramp. The gorge viewpoint is a short walk on flat ground.

options.name: Sunrise game drive
options.difficulty_note: Seated in an open vehicle, cold at first light. Bumpy.
options.description: Today we say goodbye to the Serengeti the best way possible: in the first light, when the animals are most active. The grass glows, a hot drink steams in our hands, and the plains slowly wake around us. A last drive, a last lion, and a memory to keep.
options.bring: Open vehicle: dust, sun, and cold at dawn. Layers, a hat, neutral colours. Stay seated and quiet near the animals.
options.accessibility: The vehicle has a high step (a stool is provided), and it is cold in the open air at dawn. The ride is bumpy.

options.name: Little Petra
options.difficulty_note: A short drive and about 1 km of gentle walking on sand and rock steps.
options.description: Today we discover Petra's quieter sister. Siq al-Barid, Little Petra, is a narrow canyon of carved dwellings and dining rooms where Nabataean traders once rested, and we climb a rock stairway to a painted ceiling that still holds its colours. Afterwards, a Bedouin family serves us tea in the shade. Peaceful and unforgettable.
options.bring: The sun is strong and there is little shade: hat and sturdy closed shoes. Keep to the paths and do not climb on the monuments.
options.accessibility: The canyon floor is flat, but the climb to the painted ceiling is a rock stairway of about 40 steps without handrails (optional). Partly accessible.

options.name: Petra by Night
options.difficulty_note: About 3 km on sand and uneven stone in the dark, along the 1.2 km Siq to the Treasury and back. A torch is provided. Cool at night.
options.description: Today we walk into a story told by candlelight. The Siq, the narrow canyon that leads to Petra, glows with thousands of candles, and at the end, the Treasury appears out of the dark. We sit on the ground, hear a Bedouin musician play, and drink sweet tea under the stars. Few experiences are so quiet and so magical.
options.bring: The sun is strong and there is little shade: hat and sturdy closed shoes. Keep to the paths and do not climb on the monuments.
options.accessibility: The Siq is 1.2 km on uneven sandy paving, walked in the dark by candlelight. Seating at the Treasury is on mats on the ground. Not suitable for wheelchairs. A horse or cart is available for part of the way.

options.name: Petra Siq and Treasury
options.difficulty_note: About 8 km on sand and stone with some steps. A horse ride is possible for the first 800 m. Very hot from late morning. Long day.
options.description: Today we enter the rose-red city. We walk the 1.2 km Siq, a canyon where the walls close in and the sky narrows, until a gap opens and the Treasury appears, carved into the cliff. Beyond it lie the Street of Facades, the Theatre and the Royal Tombs. This is the moment the whole trip leads to.
options.bring: The sun is strong and there is little shade: hat and sturdy closed shoes. Keep to the paths and do not climb on the monuments.
options.accessibility: The Siq is 1.2 km of uneven paving with a gentle slope, and the Street of Facades is longer. Horse carts take you to the Treasury (extra cost). Partly accessible with help.

options.name: High Place of Sacrifice
options.difficulty_note: A climb of about 200 m by 600 rock steps, in the heat, with exposed sections and no handrails. Good fitness and a head for heights are needed.
options.description: Today we climb as the Nabataeans did. A stone stairway carved into the mountain leads to a sacred platform high above Petra, and from the top, the entire rose-red valley stretches out below us. It is a hard climb and a perfect reward. Few visitors come this way.
options.bring: The sun is strong and there is little shade: hat and sturdy closed shoes. Keep to the paths and do not climb on the monuments.
options.accessibility: A climb of roughly 800 rock-cut steps, uneven and without handrails, over 2 hours. Not suitable for wheelchairs, or for guests with heart, knee or balance problems.

options.name: Marrakech City Tour
options.difficulty_note: About 4 km of easy walking with breaks, on flat stone streets and in crowded souks. Hot in the afternoon.
options.description: Today we plunge into the red city. We climb the Koutoubia minaret's shadow, wander the painted halls of the Bahia Palace, stand in the silent Saadian Tombs and then dive into the Jemaa el-Fna square, where snake charmers, storytellers and food stalls make a show of everyday life. Marrakech wakes all your senses at once.
options.bring: Crowded and busy: keep valuables close. Covered shoulders and knees are appreciated. Ask before photographing people.
options.accessibility: The Bahia Palace has uneven tiled floors and low doorways, the Saadian Tombs are on one level with a step, and the souks are crowded and cobbled. Mostly step-free but not easy by wheelchair.

options.name: Atlas Mountains Hike
options.difficulty_note: About 8 km of walking on mountain paths with a climb of roughly 400 m, at up to 1,800 m. A 1 hour drive each way. Rocky ground, some stream crossings.
options.description: Today we leave the city for the high Atlas. With a mountain guide, we walk through a Berber valley of terraced fields and walnut trees, cross a stream and stop in a village where a family invites us for mint tea and fresh bread. Quiet paths, snow-capped peaks, warm hospitality.
options.bring: Mountain weather changes fast: layers and sturdy shoes. The sun is strong at height.
options.accessibility: Paths are uneven, with stone steps and a stream crossing on stepping stones. Walking poles are available. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Moroccan Culinary Tour
options.difficulty_note: About 2 km of walking in total, in crowded lanes. Standing at a cooking table for part of the day.
options.description: Today we taste Marrakech like locals. We wander the souks, choosing spices, olives and vegetables with a chef, and then, in the kitchen of a riad, we cook a tagine and a pastilla, learning every secret. You will eat what you cooked, and you will never forget the smell of the spice stalls.
options.bring: Closed shoes in the kitchen. Tell your guide about any allergy.
options.accessibility: A walk in crowded souks, then a riad kitchen with a few steps up from the courtyard. The riad has no lift.

options.name: Farewell brunch
options.difficulty_note: Seated. No walking.
options.description: Today we end the journey the way it deserves. A long, slow brunch in a garden, with the whole group and the expedition team, and plenty of time to share the moments that mattered most. Twenty-five days, twelve countries, one table. Raise a glass.
options.bring: Smart casual.
options.accessibility: A garden on one level with gravel paths. Tables and chairs on flat ground. Step-free.
